name: TOPY.AI AI CSO skills
description: AI CSO skills for founders, built for TOPY.AI: a security officer that watches new CVEs and end-of-life dates for everything the company runs, keeps secrets out of code, checks only domains you have verified, vets every skill and MCP server before it is trusted and turns findings into plain-language fixes for a person to apply. Core skills run on the TOPY CSO MCP server (https://topy.ai/mcp/cso); standalone skills are security methods that work anywhere.

tiers.core: Runs on the TOPY MCP server; needs a TOPY account.
tiers.connected: Uses TOPY data and actions when the MCP server is connected; works on its own otherwise.
tiers.standalone: A security method that works with any agent; can use TOPY where it fits.

skills.name: Connect the AI CSO
skills.summary: Connect the TOPY CSO MCP server and check what applies: the project's stack, verified domains, granted hosts, tools and feeds.

skills.name: Daily security watch
skills.summary: Every morning: new CVEs, advisories and end-of-life dates for everything the company runs, matched to the stack — quiet unless something new needs a person.

skills.name: The CSO's goals
skills.summary: The AI CSO's standing goals and its status report for the CEO: open critical exposure, secrets in code, verified-only checks, vetted skills and MCP servers, incident timelines.

skills.name: First security setup
skills.summary: First run for a new company or site: inventory the stack, verify each domain you own, and explain host consent — so every later check is allowed and complete.

skills.name: Are we affected by this CVE?
skills.summary: A named CVE or advisory: are we affected, where, how urgent, and the response plan — with an incident timeline from start to close.

skills.name: Dependencies and supply chain
skills.summary: Known vulnerabilities in every lockfile ecosystem and in JavaScript copied into the site, prioritised, with the fixed versions.

skills.name: End of life and patch-behind
skills.summary: Runtimes, databases, web servers and operating systems that stopped (or will soon stop) getting security fixes, and what to upgrade to.

skills.name: Vet a package before installing
skills.summary: Before adding a package: known vulnerabilities and malicious-package reports for that exact version, and a clear install / pin / don't install.

skills.name: Unsafe code patterns
skills.summary: Unsafe code patterns before they ship — injection, unsafe deserialisation, personal data in logs, weak crypto — with the safe pattern for each.

skills.name: Secrets in code
skills.summary: Keys, tokens and passwords in the code, its git history and the build output — and the rotate-first fix for each.

skills.name: Threat model and OWASP checklist
skills.summary: A STRIDE threat model of the system and an OWASP ASVS checklist filled from the findings — what could go wrong and how far we meet the standard.

skills.name: Verify a domain
skills.summary: Prove the company controls a domain (DNS TXT record or a token file) before any active check — the CSO never scans a site that isn't verified.

skills.name: Headers and TLS
skills.summary: Grade a verified site's HTTP security headers and cookies (A+ to F) and its TLS (protocols, certificate trust and expiry), with the exact fix for each.

skills.name: Safe web scan of a verified site
skills.summary: A safe, rate-limited vulnerability scan (known flaws, exposed files, misconfigurations) of a site the company has verified — never exploitation.

skills.name: Audit our own MCP server
skills.summary: OWASP MCP checks on the company's own MCP tool registry: read-only hints, destructive tools behind confirmation, scopes, audit logging and hosts it may call.

skills.name: Vet a skill or MCP server
skills.summary: Before a skill, plugin or MCP server is installed or published: prompt-injection, data exfiltration, over-broad permissions and risky tools — the App Factory security gate.

skills.name: Fix plan for a person to apply
skills.summary: Turn the findings into a reviewed runbook — each action tagged T1 (batch-safe) to T4 (stage first) — that a person reviews and runs. The CSO never applies it.

skills.name: Incident timeline
skills.summary: Record a security incident or CVE response from start to close — what happened, every step and who did it — so nothing is lost and the report writes itself.

skills.name: Weekly security report
skills.summary: Every Monday: what is open by priority, what was fixed, what changed in the stack, and at most three actions — for the Founder by email and for the CEO.
